rulings.ruling: Ruling: representation; project retained. The project enters zero for a person with no Schedule C; the second applies the $400 floor of Schedule SE line 4c, which gives zero for the same person. Otherwise the same Schedule SE computation; church employee income, the optional methods and statutory employee income are refused (person.se_screen, sc.statutory), so the second's sums over all of the person's Schedules C (it no longer excludes statutory employee income) select the same entries as the project's. Railroad retirement (tier 1) compensation on line 8a is refused for a person with a Schedule C (person.se_rrta), so line 8a is W-2 boxes 3 and 7 on both sides. Both use this person's own Schedule SE line 13 (Pub. 560 p. 39, Step 2).

rulings.ruling: Ruling: representation; project retained. The project enters zero for a person with no Schedule C and otherwise the same Schedule SE computation; the second applies the $400 floor of Schedule SE line 4c (i1040sse p. 2, line 4c; 'If less than $400 ... you don't owe self-employment tax'), which gives zero for the same person. Church employee income, optional methods, statutory employees and notaries are refused on both sides (person.se_screen, sc.statutory). Both then take one-half of the self-employment tax (Pub. 560 chapter 5, Deduction Worksheet for Self-Employed, step 2).

rulings.ruling: Ruling: refusal representation; project retained. The instruction says that if any one employer withheld more than $10,918.20 the excess cannot be claimed on the return and the employer should adjust it, otherwise Form 843 (i1040gi p. 117). The project refuses the return on that condition and on railroad (RRTA) compensation through the line's `refuses` entries; the second transcription returns a zero credit. The project's reading is the spec's refusal policy (spec 2.2, 2.5); within the non-refused scope the credit agrees (eligible: more than one employer and wages over the base; excess over the limit). Stage 13 re-run: the credit is figured separately for each spouse from that spouse's Forms W-2 (i1040gi p. 117), as both transcriptions do.

rulings.ruling: Ruling: representation; project retained (as the prior ruling). Box 1 is the same on both sides. Line 1e goes to the only person whose Forms W-2 show box 10, or to the taxpayer when nobody's do, on both sides; when both spouses' do, the second now gives it to neither (and refuses, its h_dc_1e_split), where the project follows the binding reading amb.2025.dc_line1e_attribution (owner decision 6): shown in the taxpayer's line 4 and refused when a credit remains (f2441.attrib_gate). The self-employment part is the same on returns the tool completes: the second subtracts the Schedule SE deduction without a Schedule C guard (zero below the $400 floor, so the Schedule C result is used, as the project does when no Schedule SE is filed) and leaves out statutory employee income, which is refused on each Schedule C (sc.statutory). i2441 p. 4, Lines 4 and 5, "If filing jointly, figure your and your spouse's earned income separately".

rulings.ruling: Ruling: representation; project retained. Box 1 and the self-employment part are the same on both sides: the self-employment part differs only as person.eic_se does (the project's zero for a person with no Schedule C against the second's $400 floor, and the second's exclusion of statutory employee income, which is refused by sc.statutory), and both use Schedule C profit or loss when no Schedule SE is filed (p503 p. 11, Self-employment earnings, "Include your self-employment earnings in earned income, even if they are less than $400 and you didn't file Schedule SE"). Line 1e goes to the only person on a return that is not joint and to the one spouse whose Forms W-2 show box 10 on both sides. The sides differ only when both spouses' Forms W-2 show box 10: the second counts line 1e in both spouses' earned income, so it counts it twice; the project follows the binding reading amb.2025.dc_line1e_attribution (owner decision 6), refusing when line 1e is above zero and a credit remains (f2441.attrib_gate) and otherwise showing it in the taxpayer's line 4, where it cannot change the credit. i2441 p. 4, Lines 4 and 5, "If filing jointly, figure your and your spouse's earned income separately".

The self-employment part differs only as person.eic_se does: the project enters zero for a person with no Schedule C where the second applies the $400 floor of Schedule SE line 4c, and the second excludes statutory employee income, which is refused (sc.statutory); otherwise the same Schedule SE line 3 less Schedule 1 line 15, or Schedule C profit or loss when no Schedule SE is filed.

rulings.ruling: Ruling: representation; project retained (as the prior ruling). Both are W-2 box 1 plus the self-employment part, without line 1e (i2441 p. 5, Line 18, "for purposes of lines 18 and 19, earned income doesn't include any dependent care benefits shown on line 12"). The self-employment part differs only as on person.dc_earned: the second has no Schedule C guard and leaves out statutory employee income, refused by sc.statutory; below the $400 floor its Schedule SE deduction is zero, which gives the Schedule C result, as the project uses when no Schedule SE is filed.

rulings.ruling: Ruling: representation; project retained. The project enters zero for a person with no Schedule C; the second applies the $400 floor of Schedule SE line 4c, which gives zero for the same person. Otherwise the same Schedule SE computation; church employee income, the optional methods and statutory employee income are refused (person.se_screen, sc.statutory), so the second's sums over all of the person's Schedules C (it no longer excludes statutory employee income) select the same entries as the project's. Railroad retirement (tier 1) compensation on line 8a is refused for a person with a Schedule C (person.se_rrta), so line 8a is W-2 boxes 3 and 7 on both sides. EIC Worksheet B Part 1 for a person filing Schedule SE and Part 2 otherwise on both sides (i1040gi p. 47).

A distribution is refused on both sides (f8606.dist; the second's person.ira_dist_gate).

rulings.ruling: Ruling: representation; project retained. Both: covered by a plan at work (person.ira_work_plan) or by the person's own self-employed plan; the project reads person.plan, the self-employed person's own SEP or SIMPLE plan, only for a person with a Schedule C (person.ira_se_plan), where it is asked (amb.2025.ira_covered, owner decision 9(b)); the second reads it for everyone. i1040gi p. 96, Were You Covered by a Retirement Plan?, "You are also covered by a plan if you were self-employed and had a SEP, SIMPLE, or qualified retirement plan". The married-filing-separately rule in the second's note is not reached: A separate return is refused (scope.ready, s3.mfs).

rulings.ruling: Ruling: representation; project retained. Where the second caps contributions at their limits (salary reductions at $16,500 and at compensation, catch-up at its limit and the compensation left after regular contributions), the project enters the contributions and refuses any amount above the limits (person.simple_excess: catch-up above person.catchup_max, employer contributions above person.employer_max, regular contributions above compensation; person.sep_excess; and the plan screen's 'contributions that are more than the maximum deductible amount'), so the caps never bind on a return the project admits; the second now also refuses excess SIMPLE contributions (its h_simple_excess) and takes the employer contribution uncapped, as the project does. The second's compensation, Schedule SE line 4a without the $400 floor of line 4c, is never below the project's (person.se_line4c), so it admits no less. The project also enters zero for a person with no Schedule C (person.has_sc), and asks person.plan only then; a person without a Schedule C is not self-employed in scope (partnership and farm income refused by scope.schedule1), and 'If you were self-employed or a partner, you may be able to take this deduction' (i1040gi p. 93).

rulings.ruling: Ruling: representation; project retained. Where the second caps each contribution at its limit (the SEP at Step 21; SIMPLE employer contributions at the matching or 2% maximum, salary reductions at $16,500 and catch-up at its limit and compensation), the project enters the contributions and refuses any amount above the limits (person.sep_excess, person.simple_excess, and the plan screen's 'contributions that are more than the maximum deductible amount'), so the caps never bind on a return the project admits; the second's compensation, profit times 92.35% without the $400 floor of Schedule SE line 4c, is never below the project's, so it admits no less. The project also enters zero for a person with no Schedule C (person.has_sc), and asks person.plan only then; a person without a Schedule C is not self-employed in scope (partnership and farm income refused by scope.schedule1), and 'If you were self-employed or a partner, you may be able to take this deduction' (i1040gi p. 93). Evaluated stage14.simple.match_age50 ($19,662.30) and stage14.simple.nonelective_60 ($22,858.20): the second's formula gives the same amounts.

The project asks person.sav_claimed only when someone can claim the filer or spouse as a dependent (sa.dependent) and reads it only then; a person nobody can claim is not claimed on someone else's return, so the two agree on every return. f8880 p. 2, Who Can Take This Credit, "(b) is claimed as a dependent on someone else's 2025 tax return"; "is claimed" as its own per-person question is owner decision 4.

rulings.ruling: Ruling: representation; project retained (as the prior ruling). W-2 box 12 deferrals and voluntary contributions are the same on both sides. For the person's own SIMPLE salary reductions the project enters zero for a person with no Schedule C (person.plan is asked only then) and counts the whole deferral, catch-up included, refusing amounts above the limits (person.simple_excess); the second now caps the deferral at $16,500 (ret.simple_limit) because it refuses catch-up contributions rather than figuring them. A catch-up contribution is an elective deferral: f8880 p. 2, Line 2, "Elective deferrals ... to a 401(k), 403(b), governmental 457(b), SEP, SIMPLE, or the federal TSP".

rulings.ruling: Ruling: representation; project retained. The project enters zero for a person with no Schedule C; the second applies the $400 floor of Schedule SE line 4c, which gives zero for the same person. Otherwise the same Schedule SE computation; church employee income, the optional methods and statutory employee income are refused (person.se_screen, sc.statutory), so the second's sums over all of the person's Schedules C (it no longer excludes statutory employee income) select the same entries as the project's. Railroad retirement (tier 1) compensation on line 8a is refused for a person with a Schedule C (person.se_rrta), so line 8a is W-2 boxes 3 and 7 on both sides.
